title: Equipped projective analytic components and their Dolbeault quotient
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] over $\mathbf C$ [def-weil-field], with structure map $f$, and let $A$ be its smooth analytic data [def-sfb-smooth-analytic-data]. A projective Dolbeault presentation consists of finitely many connected compact Hausdorff complex manifolds $M_i$ without boundary, of possibly different dimensions $n_i$, a homeomorphism $\coprod_i M_i\cong A$, and holomorphic coordinate compatibility with the atlas of $A$. Compatibility means that on each overlap of component and analytic charts the dimensions agree and the coordinate transition is complex analytic with injective derivative. Each component has the smooth positive Hermitian metric, metric volume and canonically characterized Dolbeault operators of [def-sfb-hermitian-dolbeault-data], and its metric is Kähler [def-sfb-kahler-coordinate-data]. Specify a closed projective embedding $i:X\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^N_{\mathbf C}$ over the base, in the convention of [def-pc-projective-morphism]. Around every component point there is a nonzero holomorphic homogeneous lift $z$ of this embedding: its coordinate sections generate the unit ideal and its scheme-valued projective point equals the composite of the corresponding complex point of $X$ with $i$. The component metric is the pullback of the Fubini--Study Hermitian pairing $h_z(v,w)=(\langle v,w\rangle\langle z,z\rangle-\langle v,z\rangle\langle z,w\rangle)/(\pi\langle z,z\rangle^2)$, evaluated on derivatives of the local lift, with conjugate-first pairings. Define global smooth forms as families of the existing component smooth forms. For integer bidegrees $(p,q)$ let $Z^{p,q}=\prod_i(A^{p,q}(M_i)\cap\ker\bar\partial_i)$, let $B^{p,q}$ be the inverse image of $\prod_i\bar\partial_i A^{p,q-1}(M_i)$ under the inclusion of $Z^{p,q}$ into the family of all smooth forms, and define $H^{p,q}_{\bar\partial}=Z^{p,q}/B^{p,q}$ with its quotient map. All negative and out-of-dimension type spaces are zero. The number of components may be zero.
